notes: The sketch uses the built-in LED on D13; the external LED circuit is optional and is what is modelled here.

All are in the bottom half (bank b, rows f-j) of the upper block.
The black wire goes to the Uno GND pin next to pin 13 (in the header beside AREF), modelled as GND.1.

Breadboard hole names follow the catalogue (bank 't' = rows a-e, 'b' = rows f-j). The picture draws rows f-j on the upper half, but the names are mapped by that convention.

The button straddles the centre gap at columns 4 and 6. 1.l/1.r are taken as the upper-half (f) legs and 2.l/2.r as the lower-half (e) legs.

The orange wire joins the button leg in column 4 (4t) to the + rail, which gives the 5V side. The teal wire from pin 2 lands at 6b.i, in the same strip as the button's other upper-half leg. The 10K resistor runs from column 6 to column 9 in row c, and a black wire takes column 9 to the ground rail.
The black GND wire from the Uno is assumed to go to the second GND pin of the power header (GND.2). The 5V pin is used for the red wire.
The resistor value is 10k ohm, entered as value=10000. The built-in LED on pin 13 is part of the Uno, so no external LED is added.
Breadboard orientation in the image is flipped relative to the catalogue naming: the image's upper half (rows f-j, with the LEDs) is mapped to bank 'b' and the lower half (rows a-e) to bank 't'.
Copy 1 uses Uno pin 7 and breadboard column 7, copies 2-6 use pins 6,5,4,3,2 and columns 10,13,16,19,22 (cathode in the next column).
LED anode is the leg in the left column (bent, longer leg); cathode is the right column leg wired to the ground rail, as in the schematic.
Exact rail hole numbers (bn.3 for the Uno GND wire, bn.9/12/15/18/21/24 for the cathode wires) are approximations; the whole rail is one strip so connectivity is unaffected.
Uno GND pin used is GND.1 (the GND on the digital header next to AREF); which of the Uno's GND pins is not significant electrically.
Resistors are 220 ohm per the text. Resistor straddles the breadboard centre gap, one leg in each half. Hook-up wires modelled as jumper-wire.
Breadboard column/row positions were read from the image. The upper section of the drawn breadboard is rows f-j, so it maps to bank 'b' in the catalogue.
LED anode is the longer, bent leg in column 6. The cathode is in column 8.

Which button ports (1.l, 1.r, 2.l, 2.r) go to which legs is arbitrary, because the button's two sides are symmetric.

notes: The manual gives no wiring diagram of its own (it embeds the generic rpi-gpio-wiring-a-button guide). I used the standard wiring: each button joins a GPIO pin to GND.
GPIO pins 4, 17, 27 and 10 come from the full code listing. The manual says any pins can be used.
Button leg placement is an assumption. Each button straddles the breadboard centre gap, with 1.l/1.r in the top half and 2.l/2.r in the bottom half. Columns are 2/4, 9/11, 16/18 and 23/25.
The pin-to-socket jumper ports are named 'socket' (on the Pi header) and 'pin' (in the breadboard). The jumper-wire-mf catalogue entry lists no ports.
The 5 pin-to-socket jumpers are 4 GPIO leads and 1 GND lead to the top negative rail. The 4 pin-to-pin jumpers run from the rail to the right-hand leg column of each button.
Speakers or headphones plug into the Pi's 3.5 mm audio jack, modelled as a new 'speaker' part.
Power, keyboard, monitor and the SD card are not modelled. The software steps (pygame, gpiozero, sample files) are not hardware parts.

The text lists GPIO 25 (red), 28 (amber), 27 (green), but the Pi header in the diagram highlights GP25, GP8 and GP7 for the three LED wires. I followed the image (28 and 27 look like typos for 8 and 7).
The breadboard is drawn rotated: numbered lines 1-30 are the strips and letters a-e / f-j are the two halves. I mapped them to catalogue names as '<number>t.<a-e>' and '<number>b.<f-j>'.

The right-hand power rail strip next to the LEDs is used as the ground rail: LED cathodes, the buzzer's negative leg, the button's ground wire and the Pi GND wire all go to it. It is drawn under the '+' label, but it acts as ground. I called it 'bp' in the catalogue.

Buzzer polarity: the + marked leg goes in strip 4 (right half, j), where the blue GPIO15 wire ends in g. Buzzer port 1 is taken as +. The negative leg is under the buzzer body on the ground rail; I placed it at bp.5.
The Pi GND wire goes to the right-column pin in the GP3 row, which is physical pin 6. I named it GND.1.
Resistor values are not given, so I left them unset. The diagram shows the usual 3-band resistors.

Each resistor runs from column e of the left half to column h of the right half, bridging the centre gap. The LED anodes are in column j. The red, yellow (amber) and green LEDs are on lines 9, 15 and 21.
The button straddles the centre gap on lines 28 and 30. The ground wire is in 28d and the GPIO21 wire is in 30d. Port assignment (1.l/1.r on line 28, 2.l/2.r on line 30) is assumed.
The three LED branches differ in rows, wires and colours, so I listed them individually instead of using a repeat.
